defects.defect: Wrong date/verb: 'Columbus sailed that October, nine months later.' Columbus sailed from Palos on 3 August 1492 and LANDED on 12 October 1492. He did not sail in October; the nine-month interval from Granada (January 1492) matches the landing, not the sailing.
defects.fix: Change to 'Columbus landed in the Bahamas that October, nine months later.'

defects.location: Section 'Las Casas and the debate over Native peoples' (narrative) and Figure 2 caption, vs Worked item 3 (apush-saq-0022) part c model answer
defects.defect: Internal inconsistency on one number. The narrative says the 1791 portrait was engraved 'about 225 years after Las Casas died' and the Figure 2 caption repeats 'about 225 years after his death'. Worked item 3's model answer (bank verbatim) says 'about 200 years after Las Casas died'. Las Casas died 1566; 1791-1566 = 225 years, so the narrative is the accurate figure and the model answer's 'about 200' understates it by 25 years. A student reading the lesson then doing the worked item meets two different numbers for the same gap.
defects.fix: Align them. Either change the narrative and caption to 'about 200 years' to match the bank, or correct the bank's SAQ 0022 model answer to 'about 225 years' (more accurate, but the bank item is final and would need re-verification).

defects.location: Section 'Two ways to meet a continent', paragraph 2
defects.defect: Period error (placement). 'The French Jesuit priests tried to convert Native peoples to Catholicism, but they were more likely to spread smallpox than to win many converts.' The sentence paraphrases Princeton Ch. 6 supplement, which places it AFTER Quebec 1608. The lesson places it in a paragraph about the 1500s French model, before the sentence 'France did not found a permanent settlement until Quebec in 1608.' French Jesuit missions in North America began in 1611, after Period 1 ends (1607). As written, the lesson implies Jesuits were part of the 1500s French presence.
defects.fix: Move the Jesuit sentence to after the Quebec-1608 sentence and date it, e.g. 'After 1608, French Jesuit priests tried to convert Native peoples to Catholicism, but they were more likely to spread smallpox than to win many converts.'

defects.defect: Wrong clause: 'Smallpox reached Tenochtitlan in 1520, during the siege, and killed defenders who had no resistance, including the emperor Cuitlahuac.' Smallpox reached the city in late 1520 (Cuitlahuac died of it in December 1520); the siege of Tenochtitlan was May-August 1521. The arrival was before the siege, not during it.
defects.fix: Change to 'Smallpox reached Tenochtitlan in 1520, before the siege, and killed defenders who had no resistance, including the emperor Cuitlahuac.'

defects.location: Section 'Disease decided the conquest', Figure 3 description
defects.defect: Image description miscount: 'Four panels show the sick: one lies covered in spots while another speaks over him, and three more lie still, wrapped in blankets.' The image (u1/5s24-exam1-mcq-36.jpg, viewed) has five panels and five sick figures lying down (one spotted with a speaker over him, plus four more lying still, wrapped in blankets). Both counts are off by one.
defects.fix: Correct to 'Five panels show the sick: one lies covered in spots while another speaks over him, and four more lie still, wrapped in blankets.' Or drop the count: 'The panels show the sick: one lies covered in spots while another speaks over him, and the others lie still, wrapped in blankets.'

notes: The 110-word Cortes block quote (Second Letter, 30 October 1520) is judged ACCEPTABLE as a verbatim primary-source quotation: one coherent passage, framed by the lesson, carrying the teaching point (Cortes's words plus Montezuma's remonstrance). No trim needed.

The silver-paradox 'arms race' and 'most lasting effect' claims are NOT defects: both are in Barron's Ch. 3 in the MacDougall (1992) passage ('setting off an arms race that forced rivals to multiply their armed forces'; 'The most lasting and far-reaching effect of the increase of money in circulation was to set off...'), and the lesson attributes them to historians ('Historians argue about how far to push the argument'; 'That claim belongs to the historian who made it') rather than presenting them as stimulus fact. The earlier 0143/0144 issue was only that those claims are not in the visible stimulus — not that they are false. Naming MacDougall would make the attribution checkable; suggested, not required.
'English intermarriage was rare, so no new mixed peoples emerged' is a simplification matching the books' framing of English family settlement; noted, not a defect.
